evidence.basis: samples from the Lion's Den ore body; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: Assays of samples from the Lion's Den ore body showed 65 per cent lead, 25 ounces silver, $2.20 gold.

evidence.basis: reported two-year shipment averages; zinc uses the stated lower endpoint
evidence.verbatim_quote: The average values of the shipments of the past two years are reported to have been 45 per cent lead, 16 ounces silver, and 80 cents in gold; zinc averages 25 to 35 per cent, and in one instance ran up to 40 per cent.

evidence.basis: reported lead-carbonate ore range, lower endpoint; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: The lead-carbonate ore, it is stated, carried, besides the lead, 10 to 20 ounces silver and about $1 in gold.

evidence.basis: reported assays over 63 feet above the main vein
evidence.verbatim_quote: The country rock overlying this main vein for 63 feet is reported to have yielded assays averaging 4 per cent copper.

evidence.basis: reported grade of 5,000 tons of shipped copper ore; historic dollar values intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: The expense of exploration was covered by shipments, which included 2,000 tons of lead ore from No. 4 fault, with 5,000 tons of copper ore, reported to carry 12 per cent copper, $4 gold, and 3 per cent silver.

evidence.basis: reported average of marketed ore; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: Ore marketed in 1900 is reported to have carried on an average 41 per cent of lead, 6.33 ounces silver, and $1 in gold.

evidence.basis: reported ore-value ranges, lower endpoints; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: Its value is reported to average as follows: Lead, 30 to 50 per cent; silver, 32 to 50 ounces; gold, $3 to $4.

evidence.basis: reported widest portions of the No. 2 level northwest vein
evidence.verbatim_quote: Assays showed striking variations in values in different portions of the workings; thus, the widest portions of the vein on No. 2 level northwest are reported to have carried 625 ounces silver, and, similarly, the same level southeast to have afforded the highest gold values.

evidence.basis: reported zinc content of the mineralized bed
evidence.verbatim_quote: The values in lead and silver are so low and the percentage of zinc so high—often 32 per cent,—that exploitation of the ore for lead and silver is not at present practicable.

evidence.basis: reported grade of the principal ore lens; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: The main ore found was a small lens lying in the fissure, which is said to have yielded 20 per cent lead and $3 to $4 in gold.

evidence.basis: reported main-tunnel streak; lead uses the stated lower endpoint
evidence.verbatim_quote: The present strong streak at the face of main tunnel is said to average 50 to 52 per cent lead, 100 ounces silver, $3 in gold, and a trace of copper.

evidence.basis: reported assay of newly discovered upper-tunnel ore
evidence.verbatim_quote: It was reported to assay 45 per cent lead, 15 ounces silver, and a trace of copper.

evidence.basis: reported average of 3,954 tons of smelted dry ore
evidence.verbatim_quote: Raymond after Daggett states that 1,300 tons ran abut 38 per cent lead and 56 ounces silver, and that 3,954 tons of dry ore smelted during the year 1872 averaged 34.98 per cent lead and 51.46 ounces silver.

evidence.basis: reported assay of 360 tons extracted; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: In 1880 it was reported that 360 tons were extracted, which assayed about 95 ounces silver, 40 per cent lead, and $12 gold.

evidence.basis: reported northern-shoot assay; silver uses the stated lower endpoint
evidence.verbatim_quote: Ore from the northern shoot is said to have assayed 38 per cent lead, 8 to 10 ounces silver, $3 gold, and some copper, and the southern, or lead shoot, is said to have run 50 per cent lead.

evidence.basis: reported assay of ore above the gouge; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: Ore is said to have been taken from the quartzite overlying the gouge and is reported to have assayed 65 ounces silver, 6 per cent lead, and $3 gold.

evidence.basis: reported northeast-fissure ore; the separate contact range is not combined
evidence.verbatim_quote: It is reported that the copper-iron ore in the northeast fissure carried 15 per cent copper and that some of that at the porphyry contact carried 40 to 50 per cent copper.

evidence.basis: assay of a pure enargite specimen; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: A specimen of pure enargite from the Gemini mine was found to contain $1.65 in gold and 45.5 ounces of silver to the ton.

evidence.basis: assay of the heaviest part of a rich-ore specimen from the 1,050-foot level
evidence.verbatim_quote: An assay of the heaviest part yielded 0.77 ounce of gold and 6,980 ounces of silver to the ton, or about 22 per cent.

evidence.basis: reported average silver content of the mine's ores
evidence.verbatim_quote: The ores of the Colorado mine consisted largely of heavy carbonate with some residual galena, and their average silver content was about 45 ounces to the ton.

evidence.basis: reported assay of an oxidized copper-ore shipment
evidence.verbatim_quote: According to Mr. G. W. Riter, it contained 27.16 per cent of copper, 0.012 ounce of gold, and only 1.67 ounces of silver.

evidence.basis: reported local grade of partly oxidized Gem-channel ore
evidence.verbatim_quote: The ore was only partly oxidized but contained in places 100 ounces of silver and 1 ounce of gold to the ton.

evidence.basis: reported probable production average; historic gold value intentionally not converted
evidence.verbatim_quote: Some of the ores were rich in gold, and the production probably averages not less than $15 in gold and 15 ounces of silver to the ton.

evidence.basis: reported lower bound of the average for 22 shipments
evidence.verbatim_quote: From April 1921 to July 1927, 22 shipments of gold ore that averaged more than 7 ounces of gold to the ton had been made.

evidence.basis: reported representative 22-ton shipment
evidence.verbatim_quote: One of 22 tons in that year contained 0.02 ounce of gold and 53 ounces of silver to the ton and 47 percent of lead and is representative of the other shipments.

evidence.basis: reported average content of 786 tons shipped
evidence.verbatim_quote: From 1917 to 1920 shipments amounted to 786 tons of copper and lead-silver ore, which had an average content of 0.002 ounce of gold and 3.52 ounces of silver to the ton, 10.17 percent of copper, and 0.88 percent of lead.
